Top 5 recorded entries:

# Rationale: Default-on value refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#0 provides the current shipped status and complete default-on language set, superseding the earlier partial default-on record from the playbook.

# Default-on value refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-reference edges are enabled by default for TS/JS/TSX, Go, Python, Rust, Ruby, C, Java, C#, PHP, Scala, Kotlin, Swift, Dart, and Pascal, and can be disabled with `CODEGRAPH_VALUE_REFS=0`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#0 Status says the feature is shipped and default-on for that complete language set, with `CODEGRAPH_VALUE_REFS=0` as the opt-out.

# Default-on value refs

Lifecycle status: superseded

Value-reference edges are enabled by default for the validated language set and can be disabled with `CODEGRAPH_VALUE_REFS=0`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §1 names `valueRefsEnabled` as default ON with env opt-out, and §2 says default ON shipped for TS/JS/tsx, Go, Python, Rust, Ruby, C, Java, and C# in PR #895 and later language PRs.

# Value-ref env opt-out

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-reference emission must remain disableable with `CODEGRAPH_VALUE_REFS=0` even though it is default-on. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#0 Status says the shipped feature is default-on for the supported language set and that `CODEGRAPH_VALUE_REFS=0` disables it.

# Rationale: Whole-file family skeletonization

Lifecycle status: accepted

docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 explicitly marks per-symbol family skeletonization as future work and says whole-file skeletonization cannot express it yet, so the earlier accepted per-symbol-focused decision should not remain current.
